newsitem.title: USA: Vereinsbank plans accounts in Euro in '99.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank plans accounts in Euro in '99.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said it planned to denominate its entire balance sheet in the new European single currency, the Euro, from 1999, the launch year for the new currency.
In a speech delivered in Washington on Saturday evening, the bank's chief executive Albrecht Schmidt said, "We will draw up our balance sheet in Euro in the 1999 business year."
Schmidt said the bank planned to offer its clients the option of transacting in either marks or Euros as soon as the currency was launched.
"We will offer our customers a choice of Euro or mark for all transactions -- capital investment, financing, payments," he said.
He added that German banks appeared to be ahead of their rivals in other countries in preparation for the new single currency.
Europe plans to create a single currency in 1999 for those European nations which meet certain economic conditions.
But the size of the project means that a lengthy transition period is needed between the establishment of the currency and its general use for ordinary transactions.
Notes and coins in the new currency are set to enter circulation in the year 2002, three years after the currency's actual creation.

Schmidt said that the creation of the Euro would bring some disadvantages for banks in terms of loss of currency trading volume and reduced demand for international payments involving currency conversion.
The one-off cost of converting the bank's systems to the new currency were a further burden, he added.
"We are nonetheless confident that these losses will be offset by higher growth in the business volume in the European financial market," he said.
